correctness.rationale: The reduction of a square-zero matrix has rank at most n/2 and admits the canonical U,C,W decomposition. The count of reductions is the product of two Gaussian coefficients and GL_r(q). GL_n(R) lifts all residue similarities. In the fixed J fiber the exact equation X²=0 is equivalent to JB+BJ=0 and has q^{2r(n-r)} lifts for every B_CC. Unit-pivot elimination identifies the number of radical Smith entries with rank(B_CC), yielding the formula; all quantifiers and zero boundaries are covered. Brute-force tests for full dual-number 2×2 and 3×3 cases and mixed-characteristic Z/4 and Z/9 corroborate, but do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: This solves the complete joint invariant-counting problem (free/unit and radical Smith ranks) for all square-zero matrices over every finite length-two chain ring. The independent random-matrix conditional law and ring-universality contrast genuinely different base rings of equal residue size, including nonisomorphic F_2[epsilon]/epsilon² and Z/4. The count is a natural representation-theoretic refinement of square-zero matrix enumeration and not an arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table recalculation; the claim is restricted to its established scope.
